questions.question: Gross profit of R1 080 000 on sales of R2 880 000 gives a gross margin of:
Gross profit on COST of sales landing exactly on the intended 60 percent mark-up tells the partners:
options: Prices must be raised at once
The pricing policy was achieved — no large undetected markdowns, theft of stock before sale, or recording errors

questions.question: Net profit on sales for the year is:
An indicator only gains meaning once it is:
options: Compared — with last year, the budget, the policy or a similar business

subtopics.title: The Operating Cycle: Four New Indicators

questions.question: With cost of sales of R1 800 000 and average stock of R225 000, the stock turnover rate is:
options: 8 times a year — the shelves refill about every six and a half weeks

questions.question: The stock holding period and the stock turnover rate are:
options: One fact in two languages — refills per year against days per refill
Only comparable in a manufacturing business

questions.question: Average debtors of R61 000 against credit sales of R1 440 000 gives a collection period of:
Paying creditors at 25 days on 30-day terms means:
options: Nothing — the creditors' period carries no interpretation
About five days of free credit are being surrendered, unless an early-settlement discount justifies the speed

subtopics.title: Gearing and Return: Risk and Reward

questions.question: The debt-equity ratio of R185 000 to R889 800 is:
options: 0,2 to 1 — low gearing, light dependence on borrowed money

questions.question: A case for gearing UP exists when:
options: The bank offers a bigger loan
The business earns more on borrowed money than the borrowing costs — here, far above the loan's 12 percent

questions.question: Average equity for the return calculation is:
options: R846 300 — the average of opening R802 800 and closing R889 800

questions.question: The return on average partners' equity of 62,4 percent is judged against:
options: The risk-free alternative of roughly 8 to 10 percent in a fixed deposit — remembering the partners' labour also sits inside the return

subtopics.title: Liquidity and the Art of the Comment

questions.question: The current ratio and acid-test ratio are:
options: 4,2 to 1 and 2,0 to 1 — short-term debts covered even without selling another tin of paint

questions.question: A very high current ratio can itself be criticised because:
options: Idle cash earns next to nothing — over-liquidity wastes money that could expand the business or shrink the loan
It always means the stock cannot be sold

questions.question: The four parts of a complete interpretation comment, in order, are:
options: Figure with its comparison, trend, cause, consequence or advice

questions.question: A climbing current ratio is only good news if:
options: The debt-equity ratio climbs with it
Paired indicators like the stock holding period confirm it is not just unsold stock silting up

questions.question: The results-board picture says indicators are:
options: Small numbers standing in for a big performance, like personal bests and split times

questions.question: A policy mark-up of 60 percent with an achieved margin of only 52 percent on cost signals:
options: Stock leaking — taken before sale, quietly discounted, or misrecorded

questions.question: The coach's first rule for any number is:
options: A number means nothing alone — it needs a next-to: last year, the plan, or a rival

questions.question: The rand's lap around the business runs:
options: Shelf to promise to cash — stock, then debtors, then bank

questions.question: Whether 46 days on the shelf is acceptable depends on:
options: The trade — reasonable for paint and tiles, disastrous for fresh bread

questions.question: Paying suppliers early with no discount in return is best described as:
options: Politeness at the shop's own cost — handing back free credit

questions.question: With money out for about 61 days and suppliers paid at day 25, the gap is financed by:
options: The shop's own money — which shortening the cycle would set free

questions.question: The liquidity verdict — safe, and slightly lazy — rests on:
options: More than four times cover of short-term debts while over R134 000 sleeps in the bank earning next to nothing

questions.question: Gearing as a volume knob means:
options: Low is safe, higher is louder — the right setting depends on how steady the earnings are
The knob turns one way only

questions.question: The return of 62,4 percent against roughly 9 percent risk-free supports the conclusion that:
options: The partners should close the shop
The investment stands even after mentally pricing the partners' labour
The bank deposit was the better choice

questions.question: The four-beat bar for interpretation comments is:
